commit.message:
wallet: keep searching shielded keys while notes turn up after a restore

After a restore, the first unlock derives the shielded keys for index
0 to 19 and scans the chain once. A note on a later index is not found,
also not after rescanblockchain or a restart. Every shielded send puts its
change on a new index, so after about 20 sends the whole shielded balance
of a wallet is past that window, and the restored wallet shows 0.

Search like a gap limit: while a note turns up within GAP_LIMIT indices of
the end of the searched range, derive the keys up to GAP_LIMIT indices past
that note and scan again. Which keys are kept afterwards is unchanged.

doc: distinguish normal cloud recovery from direct seed

Refs btxchain/btx#561 and #714.
Credit to repch1c for the real-MinIO fixture and Numair for integration.

modelnet: use private directory checks on Windows

Use the existing security helper for Windows directory creation and ACL
checks rather than POSIX-only mkdir, S_ISDIR and geteuid. Translate its
typed refusals to the ensure caller error contract. Keep the POSIX body
unchanged and reuse bitcoin_model_security, already linked by ModelNet.

Builds on repch1c's directory protection in #720, incorporated as7a1360d5.
The same generated clang-cl object command fails before and passes after.
Refs #356.

doc: name the host libraries a Linux archive still needs

libevent, sqlite, ZeroMQ, and libgomp stay on the host so the archive does not carry a newer glibc. Ordinary getmodel can fill an incomplete catalog entry from configured cloud storage.

release: bundle the libraries a clean image does not have

libevent, sqlite, ZeroMQ, libgomp, and the libraries they need ship in the Linux archive. libc and the NVIDIA driver stay on the host.

release: put the CUDA toolkit library beside btxd before the Python bundle

The Python bundler reads ldd, so libcublasLt has to be in place first. The toolkit copy next to btxd is not duplicated into lib/.

swapnet: read the maker's chain clocks before the deadline check

A remote endpoint answers clock() after the time captured on receipt, so the old check treated a fresh observation as STALE_CHAIN. The quote is still checked against the receipt time. The notes also name the SwapNetHTLC creation-code hash: a runtime match does not prove the init code, and the CREATE2 address remains a recommendation.

net_processing: process unique tx INVs only

An INV message can list the same txid or wtxid many times, up to
MAX_INV_SZ (50,000) entries. Each repeat went through the whole
per-announcement path under cs_main and m_tx_download_mutex again:
AddKnownTx(), then AddTxAnnouncement(), which checks the mempool, the
recent rejects and the request tracker.

Skip an identifier already seen in the same message. Txids and wtxids
are tracked in separate sets; MSG_TX and MSG_WITNESS_TX both count as
txids, as ToGenTxid() treats them. The sets live for one message only,
so a later INV is processed normally. BTX has no SaltedUint256Hasher;
its SaltedTxidHasher (the same salted SipHash over a uint256) is used.

Test: p2p_tx_download.py gains upstream's test_duplicate_tx_inv, which
counts the "got inv" debug lines for repeated identifiers.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#35878 (original author Gregory Sanders).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

rpc: avoid descriptor range counter overflow

EvalDescriptorStringOrObject() expands a ranged scan object with
`for (int i = range.first; i <= range.second; ++i)`.
ParseDescriptorRange() accepts an end of 2^31-1, and then the increment
after the last index overflows int. That is undefined behaviour: btxd
built with -ftrapv terminates during the scan, and a normal build may
do anything (with gcc 13 at -O2 the loop happens to stop). It is
reachable from scantxoutset with "range": [2147483647, 2147483647] and
from every other RPC that expands scan objects through this function
(scanblocks, getdescriptoractivity, utxoupdatepsbt,
descriptorprocesspsbt).

Count in int64_t, so the final increment stays representable.

Test: the new rpc_scantxoutset_range_end.py checks that scans of
[2^31-1, 2^31-1] and [2^31-2, 2^31-1] return. It fails before the fix
in a -ftrapv build; a normal Release build passes either way. Upstream
adds the first case to rpc_scantxoutset.py, which stops at its first
step on BTX (it pays a non-P2MR output, rejected as scriptpubkey), so
it runs in a test of its own here.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#35872 (original author Lőrinc).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

net: treat RFC 9637 IPv6 documentation range as invalid

RFC 9637 reserves 3fff::/20 as a second IPv6 documentation range, next
to RFC 3849's 2001:db8::/32. CNetAddr::IsValid() only rejected the
older range, so addresses from 3fff::/20 counted as valid and routable:
they could be gossiped, stored in addrman and tried as outbound peers.

Add IsRFC9637() and reject it in IsValid() like IsRFC3849(). The fuzz
target now asserts that invalid addresses are not routable.

Test: netbase_tests/netbase_properties gains upstream's checks for the
range bounds and for IsValid().

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#36199 (original author Fabian Jahr).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

netaddress: make .onion suffix check case-insensitive

CNetAddr::SetTor() compared the ".onion" suffix case-sensitively, so a
valid Tor v3 address written as "....ONION" (for example in -addnode
or -externalip) was rejected, although host names are
case-insensitive and the base32 part already decodes in either case.

Compare the lowered suffix. BTX's SetTor() still takes a std::string,
so the change keeps its shape and only lowers the suffix before the
comparison.

Test: net_tests/cnetaddr_basic gains upstream's mixed-case Tor v3 case.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#36636 (original author jpk68).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address

GetLocalAddrForPeer() may adopt the address a peer reports for us
(addrMe in its version message) when that peer is routable and so is
the reported address. A peer reached over Tor or I2P cannot see our
clearnet address, so whatever it reports is either a guess or chosen to
mislead, and we could then advertise it to the network as our own.

Skip that path for peers connected through a privacy network
(IsConnectedThroughPrivacyNet()), inbound and outbound.

Test: net_tests/get_local_addr_for_peer_port gains upstream's I2P
inbound and Tor outbound cases.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#36757 (original author stratospher).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

wallet, rpc: exclude non-owned addresses from listreceivedby*

With include_empty=true, listreceivedbyaddress and listreceivedbylabel
walk the whole address book, so they also listed addresses the wallet
does not own, such as "send" entries added for payees, as if they had
received 0.

Entries in the tally are only ever added for addresses the wallet owns,
so only address-book entries missing from the tally need a check: skip
them unless IsMine().

Test: wallet_listreceivedby.py gains upstream's coverage for a "send"
address with include_empty=true.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#35925 (original author pablomartin4btc).

log: escape newlines in messages

LogEscapeMessage() escaped every control character except '\n', so any
logged text that comes from outside (an RPC method name rejected by
-rpcwhitelist, a wallet name) could carry a newline and write what
looks like a separate log line, for example a fake "ERROR: ..." line.

Escape '\n' as \x0a like the other control characters. LogPrintStr_()
first strips the one conventional trailing newline many callers still
pass, so only embedded newlines are escaped; FormatLogStrInPlace()
already appends the line terminator when it is missing.
Messages that deliberately span lines now stay on one line with \x0a
in place of the breaks: the exception banner and CommitTransaction's
transaction dump, as upstream accepted, and BTX's "MatMul RC DEGRADED
START" startup notice in init.cpp, whose options (a), (b) and (c) are
now separated by \x0a.

Adapted to BTX's logging.cpp, where escaping happens in LogPrintStr_()
rather than upstream's Format(). Upstream's functional characterization
tests in rpc_whitelist.py and wallet_startup.py are not carried: they
build on test helpers BTX's copies of those files do not have.

Tests: util_tests/test_LogEscapeMessage takes upstream's newline
expectation, and logging_tests gains
logging_embedded_newline_stays_on_one_line, which logs a message with an
embedded newline and reads back one line.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#35833 (original author Lőrinc).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

wallet: handle disabled startup settings

With -nosettings, createwallet, loadwallet and unloadwallet with a
load_on_startup value still tried to write settings.json:
updateRwSetting() called ArgsManager::WriteSettingsFile(), which throws
std::logic_error ("Attempt to write settings file when dynamic settings
are disabled.") when there is no settings path.

Only write the file when a settings path exists. The update then
reports failure, so the caller returns its usual warning that the
startup setting could not be updated, and the in-memory change is kept.

Test: wallet_startup.py gains upstream's test_disabled_settings, run
after BTX's existing load-on-startup sequence. It restarts with
-nosettings, checks the warnings for createwallet, loadwallet and
unloadwallet, checks that settings.json is unchanged, and that the
original startup wallets load again once settings are back. BTX's
TestNode.createwallet() always sends passphrase='', which adds an
"Empty string given as passphrase" warning, so the createwallet check
uses createwallet_passthrough() to send only upstream's arguments.

Backported from bitcoin/bitcoin#36176 (original author Robert Hamilton).

test: expect catch-up headers and a negotiated compact block in p2p_compactblocks

Two upstream assumptions do not hold on BTX, and the test failed at
test_sendcmpct on every head:

- After a GETHEADERS response the node records pindexBestHeaderSent,
  so the next tip takes NewPoWValidBlock's catch-up path and
  FlushDeferredFastBodies sends HEADERS and then the BLOCK, which marks
  the header as sent and suppresses the INV. The test now expects
  headers and a block (and still no cmpctblock) after
  request_headers_and_sync. It waits for the block, a separate message
  that can land after the announcement wait returns, and clears
  "block" with the other announcement messages.
- test_invalid_cmpctblock_message reconnects with a peer that never
  sent SENDCMPCT. BTX ignores a compact block from such a peer, and
  one that was neither requested nor high-bandwidth, so the too-high
  prefilled index was never checked. The test now negotiates version 2,
  requires the GETDATA to ask for MSG_CMPCT_BLOCK, and still expects
  the disconnect.

test: expect the -blocksonly ExactReplay warning in p2p_addr_relay

blocksonly_mode_tests leaves node 0 on -blocksonly=1, and
rate_limit_tests then restarts it with restart_node(), whose stop
requires an empty stderr. BTX prints an InitWarning at startup for
-blocksonly=1 (src/init.cpp): a mining or submit node that does not
relay may never deliver a winning block to the ExactReplay signer. The
stop therefore always failed with "Unexpected stderr", after the addr
checks had passed, and the rate-limit cases never ran.

Stop the node expecting that warning, then start it without
-blocksonly, so the rate-limit cases run as upstream intends.

test: expect a VERSION start height and raw-header getheaders replies in feature_block_download_slot_reclaim

The Python block sources left nStartingHeight at the framework default
of -1. btxd will not send GETDATA to such a peer:
TrustedMirrorGpuMayServeBlocks treats a negative start height as an
incomplete handshake, and SendMessages logs reason=cannot_serve_blocks.
The staller then died in P2PDataStore.on_getheaders, because block_store
holds SerializedBlock payloads with no sha256 and last_block_hash stays
empty. So the stall, reclaim and catch-up checks never ran.

Add a RawHeaderPeer that advertises the start height and answers
GETHEADERS with the headers it already announced. The staller still
records GETDATA and never sends a body; the honest peer serves the
bodies after the reclaim.

swapnet: lock reserved funding inputs again after a restart

The host re-locked its coinlocks rows while it was being built. That is
before btxd leaves RPC warmup, so the native wallet refused the call and
the BTX asset showed NATIVE_RPC in startup_errors. The rows of a swap
whose funding is already broadcast also name spent inputs, and
lockunspent refuses the whole call when one output is spent.

Re-lock from the worker's tick until it works, and lock each recorded
input on its own. A wallet that cannot be reached still fails the attempt,
which is retried on the next tick. SPECIFICATION.md already says the
coordinator re-locks still-reserved UTXOs after a restart.

wallet_swapnet_relock.py writes the two rows a funded swap leaves, one
input spent and one not, and restarts the node.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

modelnet: release a hydrated file's quarantine copy

Cloud recovery (TryHydrateFromCloud) streams each file through a
FileStreamHydration that writes every verified piece to the
cloud-hydrate-q quarantine store, and Finish copies the pieces to the
live store once the file checks out. The quarantine copy was never
removed. Each hydration opens the quarantine with the -modelstorage quota
and counts the pieces already there, so every recovered model took twice
its size on disk, and once the copies added up to the quota the next
recovery failed with "disk quota".

Drop the file's quarantine directory once the live store holds its pieces
and index, as the rejected-stream cleanup in TryHydrateFromCloud already
does for a failed file. The single-peer stream path ends in the same
Finish.

finished_hydration_releases_its_quarantine_copy hydrates two files in turn
through a quarantine that holds one. feature_modelnet_minio.py checks that
the FakeS3 recovery leaves no quarantine piece behind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: consent CR12 J02 bindings so later writes are not BINDING_REVOKED

J02 creates loopback bindings without owner consent, so they stay
PROPOSED (src/modelnet/hcp_crl12_engine.inc.cpp). The same btx-hcpd
instance then runs J03's POST /institutional/positions/batches, which
RecordBlocked refuses with HTTP 403 BINDING_REVOKED while the caller
has bindings and none is ACTIVE. That refusal is the intended access
check; the native J03 path uses a fresh engine with no bindings and
never meets it.

Send owner_consent in J02 so its bindings are ACTIVE, the lifecycle the
later journeys assume. RecordBlocked is unchanged, and J02 still checks
that another token cannot write through those bindings.

modelnet: print btx-open refuse reasons on stderr

btx-open refuses a bad local package (for example a payload digest
mismatch) with exit code 1 and a JSON error on stdout, but
PrintErrorJson wrote nothing to stderr. URI refusals already explain
themselves on stderr, and feature_modelnet_packages.py requires every
refused vector to say why, so frame-bad-digest.btxbundle failed with
"refused without saying why".

Write the message to stderr as well; stdout keeps the JSON. With
reasons visible, the test's abort ledger shows that
int-overflow-core-version.btx no longer aborts: InspectCoreVersion
refuses it with UNSUPPORTED_CORE_VERSION. Empty ABORTS_TODAY as the
test asks, so a future abort fails again.

modelnet: persist the HTLC refund terms with the funding transaction

submitmodelfunding recorded only model_output_script/_vout/_key_hash/
_release_id on the funding transaction, so the refund descriptor lived
only in the preparemodelfunding JSON the funder is never told to keep. A
funder who kept only release_id/txid could not refund a failed campaign:
exportmodelrecovery returned "no public recovery material", even with the
helper running (MergeHelperCampaign is a deliberate no-op; GAP-12).

remember_funding, which runs on every submit path, now records
model_descriptor and the refund terms and writes the wallet transaction
with an explicit WriteTx, so they survive a restart on the duplicate path
too. exportmodelrecovery recovers them from that transaction when the
options and the helper card carry none, and refuses to guess when one
release_id was funded under different descriptors. The terms are already
in the process at submit time; no consensus, fork-choice or wallet-key
behaviour changes.

test: give the funding refund recovery script a runner prefix

The functional runner only accepts example, feature, interface, mempool, mining, p2mr, p2p, rpc, wallet, and tool. The recovery check is unchanged.

swapnet: pin the open HTLC build to the Shanghai EVM

solc 0.8.24 with this profile already produced the published hashes. Paris does not. The pin keeps a later compiler default from changing the artifact.

wallet: keep shielded keys consistent when importwalletbundle replaces the PQ seed

importwalletbundle installs the bundle's PQ master seed as the wallet seed, and
shielded spending keys are derived from it. Two cases were wrong:

- Into a wallet with no shielded keys of its own, the pre-import unlock had
  already finished the empty-gap search with the old seed, so the imported
  seed's shielded notes were never searched and stayed invisible, even after a
  rescan and a restart.
- Into a wallet that already held its own shielded keys or notes, replacing the
  seed dropped the spending authority of those notes on the next reload, making
  the wallet's own shielded funds unspendable.

Decide the shielded handling on the import path, cs_wallet before cs_shielded.
If the wallet already holds shielded key material (a key set, a note, or a
non-zero derivation index), refuse before overwriting the seed and point at
restorewalletbundle; the message does not assume the seeds differ, so it is
correct for a re-import of the wallet's own bundle too. Otherwise, and only for
an encrypted wallet (only there are shielded keys derived from the seed), after
SetupImportedPQWalletBundle returns, re-check under the same lock that no key
material exists, erase the persisted shielded state (the old seed's empty-gap
result; PersistState refuses to overwrite an encrypted blob with empty key
sets) and re-derive, so the imported seed's notes appear without a restart. No
key sets are cleared.

swapnet: add the restore tool that RECOVERY.md documents

doc/swapnet/RECOVERY.md tells an operator to restore a recovery bundle
with python3 tools/restore_recovery.py --bundle ... --destination ...
--genesis ... --confirm-node-stopped, but no such tool is in the tree.
The only way to restore was to call swapnet.recovery.restore_bundle from
Python by hand.

Add contrib/swapnet/tools/restore_recovery.py with the documented
arguments. It refuses to run without --confirm-node-stopped or with a
relative path, reads the passphrase from the terminal (or the first line
of standard input), and leaves every check to restore_bundle, so nothing
is written unless the bundle authenticates and the database, audit head
and vault key check out. Point the document at the tool's path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

swapnet: re-check EVM chain identity on an interval and watch finished swaps once a minute

A SwapNet node pair polled its EVM endpoint ~1,900 times a minute after one finished swap, and ~1,200 times a
minute during it (regtest, counting proxy in front of anvil). Free public RPC providers throttled such makers
within hours (HTTP 429), so no two providers agreed anymore and swaps stalled.

- EVMAdapter.check_chain(force=False): chain ID, genesis and the contract runtime are re-checked every 300 s,
  eth_syncing every 30 s. A failed check is never cached. broadcast() checks in full (force=True) as before.
- observe(): the code at a finalized block number is read once; it cannot change there.
- SafetyPolicy.terminal_recheck_seconds (default 60): one finished session is re-observed per interval instead
  of on every one-second tick; 0 keeps the old behaviour. The execution test harness uses 0, since one tick is
  one simulated step there.

Measured with the same BTX->ETH swap: 1,201 -> 527 RPCs a minute during the swap, 1,886 -> 21 after it.
Tests: caching and expiry, full check before a broadcast, no caching of a failure, terminal interval.

modelnet: move the launch training step's working set off the thread stack

LaunchTrainer::Step() placed about 750 KiB of int32 arrays (grad is 400 KiB
alone) as function locals. Run() is called on btxd's RPC HTTP-worker threads,
and on macOS a non-main thread gets only a 512 KiB stack by default, so one
training step overflowed the stack and crashed btxd. Any RPC caller reaches it
through lab035 (lab.research_execute), including a wallet-restricted -rpcauth
user; there is no peer path. Linux and Windows give these threads a larger
stack, so they were unaffected, and the unit tests run on the main thread.

Hold the step's large buffers in a StepScratch struct allocated once per Run()
on the heap and reused across steps; the small per-token scratch stays on the
stack. Behaviour is unchanged on every platform. A unit test runs one step on a
512 KiB thread stack and requires it to complete rather than overflow; it is
not built on Windows, which has no pthread stack attribute here.

doc: point the SwapNet matrix at the posted regtest receipts

The reports name the commit and say the chain calls were real. They are not stored in this tree and they do not qualify mainnet.

swapnet: key the EVM runtime cache by block hash

A finalized block number can be replaced, so caching code by that number could accept a later block whose runtime was never checked. A forced chain check that fails also drops the previous success instead of leaving it in force.

+            if params[0] == "0x0":

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Restore an encrypted SwapNet recovery bundle into an empty SwapNet directory.
+
+Offline only: stop the native node first (doc/swapnet/RECOVERY.md). The
+passphrase is read from the terminal, or from the first line of standard
+input when that is not a terminal. Nothing is written unless the bundle
+authenticates and its database, audit head and vault key check out.
+"""
+import argparse
+import getpass
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+from swapnet.canonical import hex32  # noqa: E402
+from swapnet.errors import SwapError  # noqa: E402
+from swapnet.recovery import restore_bundle  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Restore a SwapNet recovery bundle (.snr) into an empty directory.')
+    parser.add_argument('--bundle', required=True, help='absolute path of the .snr bundle')
+    parser.add_argument('--destination', required=True, help='absolute path of the new, empty <network datadir>/swapnet')
+    parser.add_argument('--genesis', required=True, help='the locally verified chain genesis hash (hex)')
+    parser.add_argument('--confirm-node-stopped', action='store_true', help='confirm the native node is stopped')
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    if not args.confirm_node_stopped:
+        parser.error('stop the native node first, then pass --confirm-node-stopped')
+    for name in ('bundle', 'destination'):
+        if not Path(getattr(args, name)).is_absolute():
+            parser.error(f'--{name} must be an absolute path')
+    if sys.stdin.isatty():
+        passphrase = getpass.getpass('Recovery bundle passphrase: ')
+    else:
+        passphrase = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\r\n')
+    try:
+        result = restore_bundle(args.bundle, args.destination, passphrase, hex32(args.genesis.lower()))
+    except SwapError as e:
+        print(json.dumps({'error': e.as_dict()}), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    print(json.dumps(result))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())

+    with open(path, "wb") as f:

+"""importwalletbundle must keep shielded keys consistent when it replaces the PQ seed.

+keys are derived from that seed, so:

+    seed), the imported seed's shielded notes were never searched and stayed invisible. The fix
+    forgets the empty-gap result and derives/scans for the new seed, so the note appears at once.

+        w = encrypt_and_unlock_wallet(node, name)
+        z = w.z_getnewaddress()
+        fund.z_shieldfunds(amount, z)
+        self.generatetoaddress(node, 1, fmine, sync_fun=self.no_op)

+"""SwapNet re-locks the reserved funding inputs it still holds after a restart.
+
+A prepared swap funding records its wallet inputs in the coinlocks table of
+swapnet/state.sqlite, and the startup path locks them again with
+lockunspent. Once that funding is broadcast its inputs are spent, and the
+rows stay until the swap reaches a terminal stage.
+
+0.34.16 locked nothing after a restart in that window and reported a
+startup error for the native asset: the host ran the re-lock while btxd's
+RPC server was still in warmup, and lockunspent refuses the whole call when
+one output is spent.
+
+The test writes the two rows such a restart sees, one input already spent and
+one not, then restarts the node. The unspent input must be locked and the
+native asset must have no startup error.
+"""
+
+import sqlite3
+
+from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
+from test_framework.util import assert_equal
+
+SWAPNET_ARGS = [
+    "-swapnet=1",
+    "-modelbind=off",
+    "-autoshieldcoinbase=0",
+    "-regtestmatmulbindingheight=2147483647",
+    "-regtestmatmulproductdigestheight=2147483647",
+    "-regtestmatmulv4height=2147483647",
+    "-regtestmatmulrequireproductpayload=0",
+]
+
+
+class SwapNetRelockTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
+    def add_options(self, parser):
+        self.add_wallet_options(parser, legacy=False)
+
+    def set_test_params(self):
+        self.num_nodes = 1
+        self.setup_clean_chain = True
+        self.wallet_names = []
+        self.extra_args = [SWAPNET_ARGS]
+
+    def skip_test_if_missing_module(self):
+        self.skip_if_no_wallet()
+
+    def run_test(self):
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        node.createwallet(wallet_name="w", load_on_startup=True)
+        wallet = node.get_wallet_rpc("w")
+        address = wallet.getnewaddress(address_type="p2mr")
+        self.generatetoaddress(node, 110, address)
+        asset = f"btx:{node.getblockhash(0)}:0:native"
+        assert asset not in node.getswapwalletinfo()["startup_errors"]
+
+        coins = sorted(wallet.listunspent(), key=lambda c: (c["txid"], c["vout"]))
+        spent, kept = coins[0], coins[1]
+        self.log.info("Spend one input, as a broadcast swap funding does")
+        psbt = wallet.walletcreatefundedpsbt(
+            [{"txid": spent["txid"], "vout": spent["vout"]}],
+            [{wallet.getnewaddress(address_type="p2mr"): 1}], 0, {"add_inputs": False})["psbt"]
+        signed = wallet.walletprocesspsbt(psbt)
+        node.sendrawtransaction(node.finalizepsbt(signed["psbt"])["hex"])
+        self.generatetoaddress(node, 1, address)
+
+        self.log.info("Record both inputs as reserved by an unfinished swap, then restart")
+        self.stop_node(0)
+        db = sqlite3.connect(node.chain_path / "swapnet" / "state.sqlite")
+        with db:
+            for coin in (spent, kept):
+                db.execute("INSERT INTO coinlocks VALUES(?,?,?)",
+                           (asset, f"{coin['txid']}:{coin['vout']}", "ab" * 32))
+        db.close()
+        self.start_node(0, SWAPNET_ARGS)
+        wallet = node.get_wallet_rpc("w")
+
+        # The worker re-locks on its first ticks, once btxd answers RPC. Only
+        # the native asset's entry counts: an operator's own Bitcoin node may
+        # add one.
+        def kept_input_relocked():
+            errors = node.getswapwalletinfo()["startup_errors"]
+            return asset not in errors and wallet.listlockunspent() == [{"txid": kept["txid"], "vout": kept["vout"]}]
+        self.wait_until(kept_input_relocked, timeout=10)
+        assert_equal(node.getswapwalletinfo()["native_wallet"], "w")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    SwapNetRelockTest(__file__).main()
